group: Antihydra-like cryptid (4m/3, a counter that goes up on 2 residues of 3)
title: What is known about 1RB1LD_1RC1RE_0LA1LB_0LD1LC_1RF0RA_---0RC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LD_1RC1RE_0LA1LB_0LD1LC_1RF0RA_---0RC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, and reduced to a Collatz-like map. Lean proves (kernel only, halts_iff in lean/Round.lean) that the machine halts from blank tape exactly when the orbit of (8, 1) under the map (3t, k) → (4t+4, k−1), (3t+1, k) → (4t+4, k+1), (3t+2, k) → (4t+5, k+1) reaches a pair (3t+2, 0). The counter k goes up on two residues of three and down on one; along 1,000,000 rounds of the orbit its least value after round 10 is 7 and it ends at 331,763. Halting would need this upward-drifting walk to come back to 0: almost surely never, but not proved.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 42,310 cells have been visited and 24,256 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.494). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.045).

claims.title: One round, for every m and k
claims.text: From E(m,k) = 0^∞ D> 110 (10)^m (110)^k 0^∞ the machine reaches E(m′,k′) with (m′,k′) = next(m,k) for every m ≥ 1 and k, or halts when m = 3t+2 and k = 0. The start of a round (one rule per residue of m), the sweeps (three 10s of the left block become four of the right block, by induction) and the finish are symbolic runs.

claims.title: From blank tape to E(8, 1)
claims.text: After 280 steps from blank tape the configuration is E(8, 1).

claims.title: Halting is the map reaching (3t+2, 0)
claims.text: The machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of (8, 1) under next reaches a pair (3t+2, 0).

claims.title: 1,000,000 rounds of the orbit
claims.text: Iterating the map with Python big integers: no halting pair in 1,000,000 rounds; the residues of m mod 3 came 334,119, 332,791 and 333,090 times; k is 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 5, 6, ... at the first rounds, never below 7 after round 10, and 331,763 at the last round (each round is about 16/9 times as long as the one before in machine steps, so this is far beyond any direct simulation).

claims.title: Probviously nonhalting
claims.text: If the residues of m mod 3 behave like independent uniform digits, k is a walk with steps +1 (probability 2/3) and −1 (1/3): from a value k it ever returns to 0 with probability 2<sup>−k</sup>, and then halts only on residue 2. With k in the hundreds of thousands, the chance is nil; the same argument as for Antihydra.

claims.title: Does the orbit ever reach (3t+2, 0)?
claims.text: A question about the residues mod 3 of an orbit of a 4/3 map, of the same kind as the Antihydra problem; no method is known.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: Lean: halting from blank tape is exactly the orbit reaching (3t+2, 0).
Rounds of the map iterated without reaching it.
Chance the counter walk returns to 0 from k; k grows by about 1/3 per round.

sections.heading: A bouncer that multiplies by 4/3, and a counter
html:
At the end of every round the head is at the left end of the tape in state D, and the tape reads

E(m, k) = 110 (10)^m (110)^k

a block of m pairs 10 (the side that grows like the square root of the step count) and a counter of k triples 110 on the right (the side that grows like its logarithm).

During a round the block is split in two by a 110 separator, 1110 (10)^x 110 (10)^y (110)^k, and the head bounces between the left end and the separator: each sweep turns three 10s of the left part into four 10s of the right part. When the left part is down to a single 10 the round ends with m′ = y + 4. How the round starts depends on m mod 3, and that is where the counter changes:

  • m = 3t: the separator is taken from the counter, k goes down by one (if k = 0 it is made another way and k stays 0);
  • m = 3t+1 or 3t+2: k goes up by one;
  • m = 3t+2 with k = 0: there is no 110 to use, and the machine halts.

sections.heading: The map on round ends
html:
(3t,   k)  →  (4t + 4, k − 1)      (k = 0 stays 0)
(3t+1, k)  →  (4t + 4, k + 1)
(3t+2, k)  →  (4t + 5, k + 1)      halt if k = 0

Lean proves this for every m ≥ 1 and k, and that from blank tape the run reaches E(8, 1) after 280 steps; so the machine halts exactly when the orbit of (8, 1) reaches some (3t+2, 0) (halts_iff).

sections.heading: A walk that drifts away from zero
html:
Halting needs k = 0 at a round where m = 2 mod 3. Along the orbit k only came close at the very start: it is 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 5, 6, …, never below 7 after round 10, and 331,763 after 1,000,000 rounds of the map (residues 0, 1, 2 counted 334,119, 332,791 and 333,090 times, as even as dice).

If the residues are like fair random digits, k is a walk with steps +1 with probability 2/3 and −1 with probability 1/3. Such a walk started at k comes back to 0 with probability 2−k. So halting is probviously impossible, as for Antihydra; proving it would need to control the residues mod 3 of a 4/3 map, which nobody knows how to do.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.494). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.045).
After 109 steps the tape spans 42,310 cells (31,355 left of the start, 43 right), with a density of 1s of 0.573.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Antihydra-like: proved in Lean to halt if and only if the orbit of (8, 1) under (m, k) -> (4m/3 + ..., k +- 1) reaches k = 0 with m = 2 mod 3; k climbs by about 1/3 per round, and the orbit has been followed for 1,000,000 rounds.
